Headquartered in Vancouver, B.C., with satellite offices in Kelowna and Nanaimo, Kor Structural (“KOR”) provides structural engineering, consultation, design, and inspection services throughout B.C. and across North America. We deliver efficient, creative, and buildable solutions for projects of all sizes and types, including residential, commercial, institutional, and light industrial. Our expertise spans all forms of construction, including concrete, structural steel, wood-frame, mass timber and masonry.

Founded over 25 years ago by three seasoned professional engineers, KOR has grown into a team of 40+ professionals dedicated to client service, quality, and innovative building solutions. While operating as a unified, distributed team, we maintain a strong local presence. Our Okanagan office includes three Partners, while a fourth Partner oversees Vancouver Island projects from Nanaimo, along with a senior partner-led team dedicated to U.S. projects.

At KOR, we believe every development begins with a strong foundation. We bring first-class structural engineering expertise, cutting-edge technological innovation, and an unwavering commitment to your design team.

KOR’s portfolio includes diverse building types such as residential, mixed-use, commercial, office, industrial, institutional, public venues, and renovations. We collaborate closely with clients and industry professionals to integrate architectural needs into structural solutions. Committed to customer service excellence, we deliver high-quality projects that meet timelines and realize client visions. Over 25 years, KOR has designed 250+ high-rise towers across Western Canada and the Western U.S., including 24 in California, 3 in Seattle, 3 in Toronto, and 28 in Alberta.
We also have a dedicated team specializing in wood frame and mass timber and have designed over 200 projects of this type.

Structured Engineering is a purposeful marriage of creative design with efficient solutions, rigorous discipline and applied engineering principles and Building Codes. Structured Engineering means structured systems. At KOR, integrated engineering, drafting, and construction teams embrace agile workflow processes. Our efficient design solutions are creative, compliant, and economical.
KOR is constantly striving to improve efficiency and add value to clients. Our aim is to do great work and be easy to work with. Our core competencies include:
Structural engineering for a wide range of building materials, including reinforced concrete, structural steel, wood-frame and heavy timber construction, tilt-up construction, and masonry.
Design of high-rise reinforced concrete structures.
Mass timber design with a dedicated wood-frame department.
Structural plan check and peer reviews.

As part of our commitment to delivering excellent service to our clients we have developed and follow gold standard operating systems with clear policies and procedures that drive efficiency for all our projects.

Our rigorous quality control practice follows the requirements for professional practice quality management set out in the EGBC Quality Management Guidelines and includes an Independent Engineering Check of all our designs by a professional engineer who was not involved in any aspects of the original design. At KOR, we adopt:
An Organization Quality Management Policy structured from the EGBC Quality Management and Professional Practice Guidelines.
Standardized policies and procedures, and well defined and regularly monitored project workflow with rigorous quality control at all stages of Design Development and Construction Review.

We look ahead to ensure that we are prepared to meet tomorrow’s challenges. Technology is a critical enabler, and we employ both legacy and leading-edge industry software and technology to meet your needs. We use both AutoCAD and Revit/BIM, among others, to develop our construction documents and coordinate with design teams. To our clients, that means faster drawing development, improved accuracy, and real-time communication and collaboration.
We utilize state-of-the-art engineering design and drafting tools to develop and document our structural designs, including:
3D Seismic Analysis tools (e.g., ETABS and PERFORM3D Non-Linear Time History).
Finite Element Slab Design tools (e.g., RAM Concept and SAFE).
Space Frame structural analysis tools (e.g., STAAD Pro, RAM Steel, and SAP).
3D & 2D Drafting and Building information Modelling tools (e.g., REVIT, DYNAMO, BIM 360, and AutoCAD).
An internal Communication and Collaboration computer dashboard know as ‘KOR Hub,’ which provides all staff with the tools they need to execute their work.
Further, we have a Dedicated IT Department with Internal Systems Manager focused on consistency, efficiency, and continual improvement of our systems and methods.

At KOR, we don’t aim to the biggest in our field – we aim to be the best by attracting and retaining first-class talent and being a centre of excellence for structural engineering. We are a dynamic team of highly experienced professionals and skilled young talent. With 40-plus dedicated professionals on staff, KOR has expertise and experience in all typical building materials, as well as specialists available in a variety of niche fields such as Performance-based design and Peer Reviews.
John Markulin, P.Eng., Struct.Eng., PE, SE

As Senior Structural Engineer and Managing Principal at KOR, John is responsible for delivering innovative structural engineering solutions for some of the firm’s most notable projects. John is an accomplished engineer with significant project experience in the design of reinforced concrete, pre-cast concrete, cast-in-place concrete, post-tensioned concrete, tilt-up concrete, structural steel, load-bearing steel stud, wood-frame, and masonry, as well as floor systems, vertical load systems and seismic and lateral systems. From San Diego to Arizona to Whistler, his emphasis on producing project-specific and cost-effective designs that meet stringent architectural and economic constraints has helped KOR make numerous projects successful, including tall towers, mixed-use commercial and residential, light industrial warehouses, and institutional/public facilities such as ice rinks, sports facilities, and extended health care facilities, hotels, office buildings, and LEED Certified projects.

As a Senior Structural Engineer, and a Principal at KOR, Jim Manages our US projects. Jim has designed multiple developments across a variety of building types in Canada and the United States since 1988, including more than 50 high-rise projects throughout British Columbia, Alberta, Ontario, Washington, Oregon, Nevada, and California. Known for his creative structural solutions and emphasis on Customer Service. Jim uses his collaborative approach to every problem with an emphasis on client service. With over three decades of experience in Quality Control Management, Jim leads the development of Operational Quality Management Policy at KOR and is the Head of the Systems Department.

Rory serves a Senior Structural Engineer and a Principal at KOR with over two decades of experience in the construction industry. Rory leads our Vancouver Island office in Nanaimo B.C. His professional journey, marked by a unique blend of experience as a Geotechnical and Structural Engineer, has provided him with a comprehensive skillset, allowing him to tackle construction projects from their very foundations to the heights of innovation. Rory’s clients appreciate his practical understanding of construction and are confident that their business is always valued.

Kevin is a Senior Structural Engineer and a Principal at KOR. Kevin’s background in construction, beginning at an early age with his family’s construction business, along with his academic qualifications, have provided him with a thorough and practical application-based understanding of the construction industry and procedures. He has shared his concrete and wood-frame expertise on a wide variety of project types, including multi-residential and mixed-use commercial buildings ranging from low to high-rise towers. Kevin also shares with Jason in leading our specialized wood frame team.

Jason is a Principal and Senior Structural Designer at KOR. He actively leads our growing specialized wood-frame team where he shares his extensive structural design experience and thorough knowledge of various materials on multiple projects. Jason is a seasoned designer and project manager who goes above and beyond to support project milestones, maintain open lines of communication between all stakeholders, and carefully supervises all phase of his projects from preliminary design through construction and project completion. Clients value Jason’s precise knowledge of materials and Canadian Codes that are essential when designing mixed-use commercial, wood-frame residential, steel structures, and concrete buildings.

Conor is a Senior Structural Engineer and an Associate Principal at KOR, Conor has over 20 years of experience in structural engineering and has built a reputation for excellence in wood design, specializing in both mid-rise buildings and custom homes. Drawing from a comprehensive understanding of structural principles and a passion for innovative solutions, Conor delivers high-quality designs that ensure safety, sustainability, and aesthetic appeal.

Throughout his career, Conor has worked on a wide range of projects, from complex mid-rise structures to intricately designed custom homes, applying expert knowledge of wood materials, engineering codes, and modern construction techniques. This experience has honed Conor’s ability to combine functionality with design, creating spaces that stand the test of time.  With a strong commitment to problem-solving and client satisfaction, Conor is known for his attention to detail, technical proficiency, and ability to navigate the unique challenges of each project.

Omar is a Structural Engineer and an Associate Principal at KOR. Omar is a highly skilled Structural engineer with over 12 years of experience in the design and analysis of reinforced concrete buildings. Omar is licensed to practice in British Columbia and Mexico.  Specializing in seismic design, Omar has developed expertise in cost-effective, resilient structural solutions that adhere to stringent safety standards and building codes.

Through his career, Omar has successfully managed and contributed to the design, analysis, and execution of complex building projects, working on a variety of structures ranging from residential to commercial high-rises. He has expertise in the application of advanced seismic design principles, ensuring that buildings can efficiently resist seismic and wind forces while maintaining structural integrity.

In addition, Omar has a comprehensive construction skillset that allows him to bridge the gap between design and practical implementation to ensure the efficient execution of projects.  He believes in the constant collaboration between consultants, clients, and trades, delivering cost-effective, sustainable solutions.

John Bryson is a Senior Structural Consultant and Management Advisor with more than 45 years of experience. John is recognized in the construction industry for his influential roles in creative structural engineering and cost-effective design. He has designed hundreds of projects around the world including more than 200 high-rise residential buildings; 30 high-rise office buildings; 120 commercial and shopping centre type buildings; 150 wood-framed residential buildings; and more than 80 seismic upgrading projects. John is also responsible for the structural design of several projects in the Western United States and Mexico, including several high-rise residential projects in San Diego, California, ranging in height from 25 to 50-storeys.
FEATURED LARGE MIXED-USE COMMERCIAL & RESIDENTIAL PROJECTS - CANADA

We have extensive experience with large residential and mixed-use buildings and have completed 2,000+ projects of all types from concrete high-rise (over 65 stories), concrete mid and low-rise, structural steel, and wood frame projects. The following illustrates some examples of large mixed-use projects we have designed.
PARADOX HOTEL VANCOUVER, 1161 West Georgia Street, Vancouver, B.C.

Located in the financial district of downtown Vancouver, the 63-story tower is the second-tallest building in the city and one of the most iconic. The twisted hyperbolic paraboloid, design by architect Arthur Erickson and built by developer Holborn Group and TA Global, presented unique structural engineering challenges. Extensive and iterative planning and design was required to successfully achieve the various aspects of this distinctive tower.
The overall project includes market residential units from levels 26 to 63 and consists of three different floor configurations and a nine-level underground parking structure.
The Paradox Hotel Vancouver tower is tied with Altus (another KOR project) for the second tallest building in British Columbia.
STATION SQUARE, 6000 McKay Avenue, Burnaby, B.C.

Station Square is a large mixed-use development with multiple phases. Sites 2 and 3 feature 38- and 49-story residential towers integrated into a podium with retail and office space, atop four levels of underground parking. Site 4, located near the Metrotown SkyTrain and Metropolis at Metrotown, consists of a 35-story residential tower with retail and office space above four levels of underground parking. Site 5 includes a 41-story residential tower with 334 units, a three-level podium containing 40,000 sq. ft. of office space and 37,000 sq. ft. of commercial space, and a total buildable area of 308,762 sq. ft., supported by five levels of below-grade parking. Site 6 comprises a 52-story residential tower with 421 units and a three-level, 102,000 sq. ft. mixed-use podium, with a total buildable area of 408,898 sq. ft. and four levels of below-grade parking.

This development is situated adjacent to the Marine Drive Canada Line SkyTrain station and bus loop and comprises a 13-story and a 31-story residential high-rise tower connected by a two-level commercial/retail podium. The total structural area is approximately 302,206 sq.ft.

Located on the corner of Halifax Street and Willingdon Avenue in North Burnaby, this upscale, mixed-use project is poised to attract discerning renters, buyers, and commercial tenants who prioritize quality, service, and community. The development consists of two towers (60-storys and 41-storys) and will offer residential ownership, commercial opportunities, purpose-built rental and 200,000 sq.ft. of premium office space.
ONE BURRARD PLACE, 1289 Hornby Street, Vancouver, B.C.

One Burrard Place is a 55-story mixed-use high-rise with 444 residential units and three office floors, all built over 8 levels of below grade parking structure. Standing at the entrance of Downtown Vancouver, One Burrard Place is one of the tallest buildings in Vancouver, making it an iconic contribution to the skyline and giving its residents a great view of the city and surrounding BC landscape. It was the third tallest building to great Vancouver’s skyline at the time of completion. One Burrard Place meets LEED Gold Certification requirements.

This project comprises a 45-story concrete mixed-use commercial/office/residential tower, including a five-level podium with office space throughout and a rooftop deck, commercial/retail space at grade level, and approximately 327 residential market units between levels 7 through 45.
SOLO DISTRICT, Lougheed Hwy & Willingdon, Burnaby, B.C.

A Large development that comprises three high-rise mixed-use commercial/residential towers (Tower A: Cirrus – 42-storys, Tower B: Stratus – 45 Storys, and Tower C: Aerius – 52 Storys), in addition to one 49-story office/residential tower (Tower D: Altus) all over five levels of underground parking.
WEST PENDER PLACE, 1409 West Pender Street, Vancouver, B.C.

KOR was retained as the structural consultant for this mixed-use development on one of the last remaining sites in Coal Harbour, creating a contemporary landmark in Vancouver’s most prestigious waterfront neighbourhood. The development comprised one 37-story and one 11-story high-rise development. This project is LEED Silver Standard certified.
PLAZA 88, 888, 892, 898, and 900 Carnarvon Street, New Westminster, B.C.

Four high-rise residential towers, ranging in height from 27 to 38-storys, with a very large commercial development, including Safeway grocery store, Shoppers Drug Mart, two banks, a liquor store, restaurants, a twelve theatre Landmark Cinemas, and numerous other commercial tenants. The commercial levels are integrated with the existing Translink station platforms.
RIVER DISTRICT (PARCEL 17), 8538 River District Crossing, Vancouver, B.C.

19-story high-rise tower and separate 8-story mid-rise tower with several townhomes along Marine Way. This project includes 296 residential units total, and approximately 53,200 sq.ft. of commercial/retail space at grade level (including a 43,300 sq.ft. grocery store, a bank, a coffee shop, and a restaurant), all built over three levels of below grade parking structure. The total gross buildable area is approximately 354,600 sq.ft.

32-story residential high-rise tower including 82 market residential condominiums (two, three, and four-bedroom) on Level 9-32 and 44 social housing units (studio, one, two and three-bedroom), ownership of the which will be transferred to the City of Vancouver prior to completion. All built over four levels of below grade parking structure for 156 vehicles and 158 bicycles. The total gross buildable area is 178,812 sq.ft. This project is being deigned to LEED Gold Standard.

This project comprised three mixed-use commercial and residential buildings, including one 14-story tower (Building A), one 5-story tower (Building B), and one 9-story tower (Building C) all over two levels of underground parking.
AQUILINI CENTER SOUTH TOWER, 685 Pacific Boulevard, Vancouver, B.C.

One of the three towers built along the perimeter of Rogers Arena, Aquilini Centre South stands at 30-storys and is primarily residential with 270 units. Designed by FRANCl Architecture and built by Aquilini Investment Group, Aquilini Centre South is on the edge of many neighbourhoods, such as Yaletown and Gastown, giving its residents great access to all Downtown Vancouver.

NUVO is a sophisticated 44 story residential condo tower located in a serene Parkside enclave within Burnaby’s cosmopolitan Metrotown. It offers approximately 358 efficiently planned studio, one, two, three bedrooms condos and townhomes in addition to 12,000 sq.ft. of indoor and outdoor amenities curated for social and health wellness. The elegant architecture design of the tower was inspired by the natural beauty of nearby Central Park.
THE JERVIS, 1171 Jervis Street & 1305-1315 Davie Street, Vancouver, B.C.

This project comprises a 19-story mixed-use commercial and residential building with a three-level podium structure. The podium structure includes one commercial retail unit at grade level and 23,641 sq.ft. of social housing. The tower levels include 58 design-led market residential condominiums (two and three-bedroom). The total FSR is 113,981 sq.ft. All built over three levels of below grade parking structure
LOUGHEED HEIGHTS, 515-525 Foster Avenue & 655 North Road, Coquitlam, B.C.

Lougheed Heights is a mixed-use development that comprises one 37-story residential tower (Tower 1) with four attached townhouses and two-story amenity building at grade level; one five-story rental building with 57 residential units; one 29-story residential tower (Tower 2) with three attached townhouses at base; and one 28-story residential tower (Tower 3) with commercial space and three attached townhouses at grade level, all over four levels of underground parking.

The Offices at Burrard Place is one of the four towers in the Burrard Place precinct and, standing at only 13-storys, is the lowest of the four. The building has over 140,000 sq.ft. of office spaces, and access to amenities such as a fully equipped gym, full-sized pool, sauna, hot tub, yoga room, lounge, and many others. Designed by the renowned architect Bing Thom, The Offices at Burrard Place is inspired by the folding pages of a book, transcending the ordinary and bringing vitality to surrounding areas.
KINGS CROSSING, 7358 Edmonds Street, Burnaby, B.C.

Kings Crossing is a master-planned community located in Burnaby’ s Edmonds Town Centre and constructed by Cressey. This mixed-use development combines a pavilion-inspired office tower, 70,000 sq. ft. of grocery-anchored retail and 3 residential towers (36-storys, 30-storys, and 27-storys) with nearly 800 units, all over five levels of underground parking. Kings Crossing is located at the high traffic intersection of Kingsway and Edmonds Street.
MAHOGANY AT MILL LAKE, 2180 Gladwin Road, Abbotsford, B.C.

26-story mixed use residential/office tower with three levels of office space at grade level and residential space above, all over two levels of below grade parking structure. The total gross buildable area is approximately 216,614 sq.ft.
THE CHARLESTON, 1396 Richards Street, Vancouver, B.C.

The Charleson is a 43-story premium residential and mixed-use tower located on the north side of Vancouver’s False Creek. The building’s appearance has been strongly influenced by neighbourhood in which it resides as well as the building’s orientation. The building takes its name from the Charleson Park view cone, which also defines the triangular tower form. It embodies the high-quality aesthetic associated with contemporary urban living. There are two main elements to the building: a low-rise rental podium and a market residential tower. There is also a strong public arts amenity component to the project.
Sovereign is a 45-story mixed-use high-rise building with 202 residential units starting at the 20th floor, as well as retail and office space below, all over five levels of underground parking.

This is one of KOR’s elegant designs that reflects the intimate relation between architectural beauty and structural excellence. It includes three above-grade superstructure ‘blocks.’ The West block is an 11-story residential tower, and the East block is an 8-story mixed-use retail and office tower, connected by an 8-level residential Skybridge that spans across/between the East and West blocks, all built over four levels of underground parking structure.

The Vue is a 44-story mixed-use building with six and half levels of below-grade parking and a separate six-story wood-frame rental residential building built over two levels of below grade parking structure.
MIRABEL, 1345 Davie Street & 1180 Broughton Street, Vancouver, B.C.

This project comprises two high-rise residential towers (East Tower: 18-storys and West Tower: 19-storys) connected by a four-level podium and includes 68 social housing units in the podium levels and 148 market residential units between the two towers. The total gross buildable area is approximately 229,716 sq.ft. The entire project is built over four levels of below grade parking structure.

This project comprises a two-tower development with a 35-story market residential tower and a 22-story rental residential tower. The Hensley is set to be a landmark in the area with distinctive columns that zigzag up the entire height of the tower. Both towers are built over four levels of below grade parking structure.
THE STANDARD, 6468 & 6420 Willingdon Avenue, Burnaby, B.C.

A 43-story concrete market residential tower with 3-level townhouse podium and 424 residential units total, plus a separate 6-story wood-frame rental residential building with 92 affordable housing/rental units, all built over four levels of shared below grade parking structure. The total gross buildable area is estimated to be 436,658 sq.ft. It is currently under construction.
CENTERVIEW PLACE, 1308 Lonsdale Avenue, North Vancouver, B.C.

This project comprises one 18-story and one 24-story residential/commercial building, with two levels of commercial space (including a 36,000 sq.ft. grocery store) and a 4-story office building, all over four levels of underground parking. The structural slab area is approximately 900,000 sq.ft.
CROWN, 520 Como Lake Avenue, Coquitlam, B.C.

A 26-story residential high-rise building, including approximately 180 residential units, plus seven 1 and 2 story townhouse units. The tower includes two levels of above grade parking within the three-level podium, as well as four levels of underground parking. Total gross buildable area is approximately 163,484 sq.ft.
FIRST PLACE, 188 East 1st Avenue, Vancouver, B.C.

First Place is an 11-story concrete residential tower, including 148 residential units for the Atira Women’s Resource Society, built over one level of underground parking. This building is LEED Gold Standard Certified.

Avalon 3 is a concrete building consisting of 329 residential units across a 26-story tower, a 6-story mid-rise, and a collection of townhouses. The building features a 20,000 sq.ft. landscaped courtyard, a 10,000 sq.ft. rooftop podium, an indoor and outdoor lounge, a pool, a hot tub, a fitness facility, and two levels of underground parking. The contemporary design by IBI Group Architects utilizes contrasting dark grey and white brick with varied panelling, making Avalon 3 a striking addition to West group’s River District community.
PARK ROYAL TOWERS, 752 Marine Drive, West Vancouver, B.C.

Three ‘blocks’, including a West and East Block located within the jurisdiction of the District of West Vancouver, and an adjacent South Block located on Squamish Nation land. The two tower buildings include 201 residential dwelling units (103 units in the 14-story ‘East Tower’ and 98 units, including 11 supportive housing units, in the 11-story ‘West Tower’). The project also included 29,000 sq.ft. of commercial/retail space at grade level and Level 2, plus a 3,000 sq.ft. childcare facility. All built over 3 levels of below grade parking.
THE SMITHE, 885 Cambie Street, Vancouver, B.C.

The Smithe, found in Yaletown, is a 27-story high-rise with 34,000 sq.ft. of office and retail space, 92 residential units, and six levels of underground parking. The design by GBL Architects and built by Boffo Developments has received LEED gold certification and offers its resident an elegant living experience.

Addition is a 20-story residential tower with 164 residential units, including six 3-level townhouses at grade level, directly built over four levels of below grade parking structure. The total gross floor area is 142,508 sq.ft.
This project comprises two curvy concrete towers; one tower is 32-storys, and the other is 26-storys.
VETERANS VILLAGE, 10626 City Parkway, Surrey, B.C.

The project comprises a 20-story concrete mixed-use residential and office tower with approximately 196 residential units, 41,296 sq.ft. of office space, a 7,000 sq.ft. Legion, and 29,000 sq.ft. of amenity space. The total gross buildable area is estimated to be 205,394 sq.ft. All build over six levels of below grade parking structure, including 381 parking stalls.

Our team has extensive experience in designing both 5-storey and 6-storey wood-frame buildings, so we are experts in special design issues related to these structures. The Building Code prohibits shear wall transfers in wood-frame buildings over 4-storeys, hence we recommend consulting with us early during initial schematic design, so that important shear wall elements can be integrated into the unit plans and overall building massing.
The following is a sample of some wood-frame residential and townhouse projects we have designed.
COLTON, 20144/20148/20276 86 Avenue, 8539 201B Street & 20129 85 Avenue, Surrey, B.C.

A mixed-use development featuring five 6-storey apartment buildings, a 3-storey amenity building, and a staggered six-level underground parkade on a sloped site. Level P3 has split floors and a recessed center, providing a 17 ft. clearance for trucks. The parkade spans approximately 362,833 sq. ft.
HOY CREEK HOUSING CO-OP, 2905 Glen Drive, Coquitlam, B.C.

A six-storey wood-frame residential building with 132 co-op housing units and two levels of below grade parking structure. The gross floor area for the project is estimated to be 113,500 sq.ft. Hoy Creek is currently under construction.

A single 6-storey wood-frame condominium development with 61 units, including studio, 1, 2, and 3-bedroom homes, all built over two levels of below grade parking structure. Currently under construction.
Two 4-storey wood-frame residential buildings with a combined total of 104 units built over one level of below grade parking structure. Construction is complete.
NSDA Architects for the Kekinow Native Housing Society
THE BEAUMONT, 1490 West 32nd Avenue, Vancouver, B.C.
4-storey multi-family residential development with approximately 81 rental residential units, including bachelor to 4-bedroom homes, all built over one level of below grade parking structure.
LITTLE MOUNTAIN (BUILDING EA), 4902 James Street, Vancouver, B.C.

A six-storey wood-frame residential with one level of below grade parking structure for storage space and approximately 56 vehicles. The project includes approximately 69 one to three-bedroom social housing (non-market) units for BC Housing, and an estimated total gross floor area of approximately 80,238 sq.ft.
LAKESIDE PLACE, 805 Nelson Avenue, Nelson, B.C.
A four-storey residential retirement home, which includes a mix of studio, one & two-bedroom homes and on level of below grade parking structure. Construction was completed in 2022.
CHELSEA MARINE, 95 & 75 SW Marine Drive, Vancouver, B.C.
Two 6-storey wood-frame residential buildings with 102 affordable housing units for the Vancouver Affordable Housing Agency. The two buildings are built over separate underground parking structures.
CLYDE, 3229 St. Johns Street, Port Moody, B.C.

Clyde is a contemporary 6 storey wood frame development offering 117 homes. All homes have generous outdoor space, and the penthouse level homes feature private rooftop decks. There is retail space along the ground level along St. Johns. The project is built around a private courtyard. Indoors, there is a fitness centre and a lounge and party room.
